extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for humanities and social-science journals (Cambridge Public Humanities and similar journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for conducting peer review of humanities/social-science manuscripts, assessing argument, sources, methods, literature engagement, prose, and recommending accept/revise/reject.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether examples and arguments in papers are compelling — do they advance the case?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the evidence and examples meaningfully support and advance the author's central claims; point out where claims feel unsupported or where evidence does not strengthen the argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Well-reasoned
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the argument is well-reasoned — does the argument follow logically?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify logical gaps, unwarranted inferences, or places where the reasoning leaps; recommend where additional premises, evidence, or clarification is needed for logical coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: True (accuracy of claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether empirical/textual claims are true — are the empirical/textual claims accurate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check factual, archival, and textual assertions for accuracy; note errors, misreadings, or overstated claims and suggest corrections or sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it is clear what the authors want to communicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out confusing passages, unclear terminology, or structural issues that obscure the manuscript's aims; suggest reorganization or rewriting where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understandability of aims and conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the main aims and conclusions are understandable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the thesis and conclusions are explicitly stated and follow from the evidence; recommend clearer statement of aims or more explicit linkage between evidence and conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution to existing literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews should explain the manuscript's contribution to existing literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Situate the manuscript relative to major works and debates; explain whether and how it advances, revises, or challenges existing scholarship and suggest missing comparative citations if relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of manuscript's aim
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript's aim should be defined consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for shifting aims, mixed scopes, or internal contradictions; recommend aligning statements of purpose throughout the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of main argument
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewer should identify the manuscript's main argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize the central claim in the review to demonstrate understanding and to assess whether the manuscript supports that claim adequately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify its methods (interpretive, archival, theoretical).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the methods are appropriate and clearly described; note missing methodological detail or unacknowledged methodological limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization within scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: How these are situated within current scholarly literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the author engages relevant debates and literature; point out omissions, mischaracterizations of literature, or overstated novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and secondary scholarly contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: The project's primary and secondary scholarly contributions should be identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish main contributions from supplementary ones and judge whether the claims about contribution are supported by the work presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Up-to-date literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Cited studies should be an up-to-date representation of current knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag outdated or incomplete bibliographies; suggest recent scholarship to include and note whether the literature review reflects current debates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards of the field
rubrics_metrics.description: The overall approach should meet the standards of the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge methodological rigor, evidentiary standards, and argumentative practices against disciplinary norms; indicate departures and whether they are justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement with debates and competing positions
rubrics_metrics.description: Engagement with major debates and competing positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how the manuscript addresses counterarguments and alternative interpretations; suggest additional engagement with prominent opposing views where needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate use of primary sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether primary materials are selected and used appropriately to support claims; note missing primary evidence or misuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of archival material
rubrics_metrics.description: Proper handling of archival material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess archival methodology, provenance awareness, citation of archival sources, and whether archival claims are substantiated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretive soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound interpretive approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate interpretive moves for plausibility and restraint; note overinterpretation, speculative readings presented as fact, or insufficiently justified interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of theoretical framework
rubrics_metrics.description: Theoretical framework explicitly stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the author states and situates their theoretical approach; assess whether the framework is appropriately applied and its implications acknowledged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-blind review protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review in the humanities is predominantly double-blinded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow journal anonymity protocols when preparing comments; avoid identifying the author or revealing your identity in review text or file annotations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turnaround expectations (time)
rubrics_metrics.description: The review process tends to last longer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of longer expected timelines for thorough humanities reviews; communicate promptly about delays and provide sufficiently detailed feedback within expected schedules if possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on prose and argumentation
rubrics_metrics.description: More emphasis on prose and argumentation than on statistical methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give detailed attention to writing quality, clarity, rhetorical structure, and argumentative presentation; provide line/paragraph-level suggestions when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerance for theoretical/interpretive frameworks
rubrics_metrics.description: More tolerance for theoretical/interpretive frameworks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect diverse theoretical approaches while assessing coherence and rigor; avoid dismissing unfamiliar frameworks without substantiated methodological critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation accuracy when foreign-language sources are used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check translations cited or used; flag mistranslations, ambiguous renderings, or lack of original-language citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hermeneutic care
rubrics_metrics.description: Hermeneutic care in interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect careful, context-sensitive readings; flag anachronistic or decontextualized interpretations and suggest more historically grounded readings where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical contextualization of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical context of textual evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether texts or artifacts are situated within their historical contexts and whether contextual claims are supported by evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disciplinary conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary conventions (citation style, tone, length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the manuscript meets the journal/discipline's stylistic and formal norms; note deviations in citation format, tone, or length and whether they are justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice and authorial style
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice and authorial style — humanities reviewers may comment on prose more extensively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate appropriateness of authorial voice and stylistic choices for the intended scholarly audience; recommend edits for clarity, voice consistency, and register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical decisions: Accept; Minor revisions; Major revisions / Revise & Resubmit; Reject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear recommendation and justify it with evidence-based reasons; when suggesting revisions, indicate whether changes are minor or major and, where appropriate, provide paragraph-by-paragraph commentary.
